warning_review.author: /root/review_gc
accepted_design: Root run-conformance setup enables warn('@on') before native counterparts and selected upstream execution, preventing the initial off state from hiding unexpected warnings.
The retained global __gc object stays rooted until state closure. Requiring stdout OK in the shutdown negative distinguishes top-level completion from an earlier script error.
Default warnings preserve normal process success but must be rejected by the scoped empty-stderr criterion. The real T warning handler rejects unexpected warnings as a process failure.
Explicit @off remains a successful control. Fragmented @store publication, exact _WARN content, explicit consumption and restoration to @normal are checked.

Timeout, capture overflow, pipe-drain failure and process-tree kill failure are rejected. Diagnostic substring requirements prevent a missing executable/library alone from being mistaken for a successful warning negative.

findings.finding: A matching diagnostic plus any nonzero exit is accepted, including a crash after emitting that diagnostic. Default normal-warning does not require top-level OK either.
findings.required_resolution: Require the known normal/default zero exit and OK, C test handler EXIT_FAILURE, and the actual Ada abort status for the platform; reject unrelated termination statuses while retaining the diagnostic and shutdown-order checks.

findings.finding: The index records arguments, executable/capture hashes and results but no repository/source/library identity. The parent GC/events index does not hash-link this warning index; the main runner source list omits both warning/hook scripts.
findings.required_resolution: Bind the warning evidence to its source/revision/library identities and retain a hash link from the parent campaign. A passing local output alone must not become final-revision warning evidence.

inspected_evidence.actual_results: Six default C/Ada cases exit zero; warning negatives have the expected diagnostics and shutdown OK. Eight instrumented cases show C warning failures exit 1, Ada Windows warning failures exit 3; explicit-off and consumed-store controls exit zero. All retained stdout/stderr hashes match.
inspected_evidence.limitation: These are local Windows observations of the reviewed draft; they do not establish Linux/macOS or complete scoped coverage.

warning_revision_review.author: /root/review_gc
rationale: Default negatives now require exit zero and top-level OK, while still requiring the specific warning diagnostic and rejecting empty stderr. A warning followed by an unrelated abnormal exit is no longer accepted.

The C T failure matches pinned ltests.c badexit EXIT_FAILURE; the Ada handler matches its explicit abort path (Windows 3, supported POSIX Process.ExitCode 134). Unexpected termination codes are rejected in addition to process/capture failures and missing diagnostics.
The retained-global shutdown case still requires OK before its finalizer diagnostic. Explicit off and fragmented store-consume-normal positive controls remain zero-exit/empty-stderr checks.

The warning index now binds repository revision/dirty state, six source hashes, actual runtime/reference library hashes, executable hashes, exact command arguments and capture hashes. The GC/events campaign index links it by path and hash. A partial or failed warning run cannot produce successful later file observations because the hook throws before those executions.
warning_revision_review.verification: Independently rehashed all 14 cases' stdout/stderr captures and both reviewed script identities in the recorded source lists. Observed default exits are zero, C T negatives one, Ada Windows T negatives three, and positive controls zero. No Alire build or source change by this cross-reviewer was needed.
limitations: Local evidence records a dirty implementation checkout honestly; final clean revision and all platform executions remain required.
POSIX abort-status handling is a fail-closed expectation derived from abort/SIGABRT and the process runner, not a claim that the newly added tests have already passed POSIX CI.
This accepts the warning regression changes and provenance design, not complete scoped or full-M3 acceptance.

capability_review.author: /root
capability_review.rationale: Has_Nonblocking_Pair reads callback 16 independently from failing-stream callback 15. The native dispatcher supplies 16 only on Windows, so pair/protocol tests cannot run on macOS merely because a failing-stream fixture exists there. Shared file validation and zero-byte refusal tests remain selected on both supported hosts. Buffered-close expectations are explicitly separated by native capability rather than suppressing a failing test.
capability_review.limitation: This accepts the capability/registration correction, not the inferred Darwin close behavior. The Darwin test and three-span equivalent still need actual native C/Ada execution before semantic acceptance.
